question: Should the experimental Claws lifecycle ownership model become a core doctor surface after the prerequisite stack lands?
rationale: This PR adds a new core lifecycle capability defined by an open RFC, and neither the experiment gate nor implementation quality establishes permanent product ownership or support expectations.

options.title: Sponsor the core diagnostics surface
options.body: Accept the experiment-gated core direction after the non-mutating state path, prerequisite contract, and real proof are complete.

options.title: Defer with the full RFC stack
options.body: Keep this PR open but unlanded until maintainers evaluate the prerequisite and subsequent Claws lifecycle slices together.

options.title: Decline the core lifecycle direction
options.body: Close the implementation stack if maintainers do not want Claws ownership and reconciliation to become a core OpenClaw capability.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core diagnostics surface
recommendation.body: Accept the experiment-gated core direction after the non-mutating state path, prerequisite contract, and real proof are complete.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent shared-state migrations and doctor safeguards make Peter the strongest available owner for deciding whether this persistent lifecycle model belongs in core and what non-mutating contract doctor must uphold.
